summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause with limited incidents: the US carried out what it called limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran is still attacking ships around the strait, and the US blockade of Iranian ports continues while indirect talks go on. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: US officials said the US carried out limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 2, after Iranian surface-to-air missile threats; they said it was not a resumption of major combat (Wall Street Journal, then Reuters). Indirect talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough announced; Vice President Vance said there has been progress.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent closed Friday, Nov 6, just under US$99 a barrel and WTI under US$91, both down about 12% to 13% on the week, the biggest weekly drop since 2022 (Rigzone), on hopes that the US election result brings an Iran deal; Thursday Brent had settled at US$98.29 after more tanker attacks (EnergyNow; Rigzone; Nation Thailand).

updates.text: Qatar's prime minister urged the US and Iran not to wait for a 'perfect moment' to reach a deal to end the war and said the US is willing to seek a solution.
sources: Al Jazeera: Iran war live, Nov 7

updates.text: Iran's navy said in a statement on Saturday that an oil tanker it said had switched off its navigation systems in a prohibited area struck a sea mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, caught fire and was immobilized; it did not name the ship.
sources: Tasnim News Agency: Violating tanker hits sea mine in Strait of Hormuz
AP (via ClickOnDetroit): Iran says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on missile ranges

updates.text: Revolutionary Guard spokesman Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said at a Tehran news conference that Iran's self-imposed 2,000 km limit on ballistic missile range had been lifted; AP noted Iran is not known to have missiles beyond that range.
sources: AP (via ClickOnDetroit): Iran says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on missile ranges

updates.text: The Greek manager Velos Tankers said a seafarer was killed on Thursday when what it called an apparent missile struck its empty tanker Velos Sapphire in the Persian Gulf; separately, UKMTO said on Friday a tanker leaving the strait off Oman reported an explosion at the waterline, with the crew safe.
sources: CBS News (via Yahoo News): Trump touts imminent decision on potential new attack on Iran
The New Indian Express (via ripr.trade): Sailor killed in Gulf as Iran says tankers on fire

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state media on Friday that two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in and near the Strait of Hormuz; CBS News noted no confirmation of these incidents from maritime officials.
sources: CBS News live updates: More ships attacked in Persian Gulf

updates.text: President Trump said the US may have to 'destroy' the rest of Iran and that people would 'know soon enough' if he acts; Al Jazeera reported that Iran has sent a nuclear proposal to the US through Qatari mediators, which Washington is reviewing.
sources: Al Jazeera live: Trump warns US may have to destroy rest of Iran

updates.text: Reuters reported that Iran said three more tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday; UKMTO said at least five vessels have reported incidents since Sunday and counted 35 vessels hit in October, the most of any month of the war. Neither side has announced a breakthrough in the talks with Qatari mediators.
sources: Reuters via Investing.com: Tankers hit in Hormuz as Iran keeps up pressure after US vote

updates.text: US officials told Axios that military preparations for a possible resumption of major combat are being completed, which is not an order to strike; separately, Qatari mediators are seeking US and Iranian backing for a draft deal that could restart direct talks within days, with Iran reportedly demanding an end to the US naval blockade and sanctions relief before reopening Hormuz (Gulf News live updates).

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
